title: A Data-Centric Hardware Accelerator for Efficient Adaptive Radix Tree
problem: Adaptive Radix Tree (ART) operations suffer from redundant tree traversals and high synchronization costs during concurrent read/write operations in databases and key-value stores.
motivation: ART is widely deployed in modern systems, but concurrency overhead and traversal redundancy significantly degrade throughput in multi-threaded workloads.
method: Proposes DCART, a data-centric hardware accelerator that exploits temporal and spatial similarities in workloads; coalesces operations targeting the same ART nodes and adaptively caches frequently traversed nodes and their search results.
key_novelty: Data-centric processing model for ART acceleration that coalesces operations and adapts caching based on runtime access patterns.
contributions: Data-centric processing model coalescing operations on the same ART nodes
Adaptive caching of frequently traversed ART nodes and search results
21.1x-44.2x speedup and 71.1x-148.9x energy savings on Xilinx Alveo U280 FPGA
limitations: Not discussed—no analysis of memory footprint or scalability to different ART configurations.
primary_theme: Data-centric ART acceleration via operation coalescing and adaptive caching
